$comment: Machine-readable migration state, one entry per domain area. Read by tests/parity/ownership-guard.mjs and, from session 2 onward, by site/erp-bridge.js. Update this file in the SAME commit that changes an area's owner — never lag behind the code.

owner.engine: Fully implemented in site/erp-engine.js today; erp.html reads/writes it directly or via ErpBridge pass-through.
owner.factory: Implemented as a packages/ capability, reached through site/erp-bridge.js. erp-engine.js may still hold a shrinking legacy copy during transition; erp.html must not call it directly once an area is 'factory'.
owner.unbuilt: No implementation anywhere yet (neither erp-engine.js nor packages/). Net-new capability work.

$schema.specSection: Section number in Requirements/20260731_REQUERMIENTOS BÁSICO CANEI.docx this area corresponds to.
$schema.engineSection: The section-divider comment in site/erp-engine.js that implements this area today, or null if unbuilt.
$schema.plannedSession: The session number (see the plan) expected to move this area to its next owner state.

budgets-versions.note: Session 9 built the three-zone constructor of §3.3 (chapter/line tree, editable grid, live totals panel) but deliberately did NOT move this area: the constructor is a view, and every figure it shows — line amounts, chapter subtotals, base, tax, withholding, total, margin, the value of the lines still pending a price — is asked of erp.budgetTotals(), the same function the emitted document uses. That is what makes the panel genuinely live rather than an optimistic copy that drifts from the document by a cent. The grid edits through erp.editLine(), which goes through _editableVersion, so a frozen, issued or accepted version refuses the edit. plannedSession is null because there is no pending move: totals and versioning are correct where they are, and a capability would be a rewrite for its own sake.

budget-graphic-annex.note: Owned by @repo/capability-docs (src/annex.ts) and reached only through site/erp-bridge.js (ErpBridge.docs.annex). The capability decides the whole layout — grouping and ordering by chapter then line number, the correlative numbering when a line has several pictures, the pagination at N per page, and which rows carry the discreet reference mark — from a list of images it is handed; it never touches bytes and never decides eligibility. The engine keeps what is genuinely its own: the image records on a line, the per-budget switch, and the fact that issuing a version snapshots the annex settings onto it so a sent document can always be reproduced. Bytes live in the blob store under storageKey (session 3's rule: binary never enters the state blob), compressed by the host before they are stored. Internal-only images are dropped at the document boundary by renderBudgetDoc, alongside cost and margin — a value that never enters the customer document cannot leak out of one.

projects.note: Session 10a built the persistent project selector and the fixed header of §4 (one context for every subsection, so two screens can never show different jobs at once) and added progress by executed quantity, per-chapter progress, committed cost per chapter and the stored forecast overrides. The area stays engine on purpose: the frozen baselines, the numbering, the acceptance-to-project inheritance and the cost ledger are all correct where they are, and the two derivations that genuinely did not exist — the plan from the budget, and cost at completion — went to capabilities instead. Moving the rest would be a rewrite for its own sake.

change-orders.note: Session 10b added the step §4.5 actually asks for — sendChange (priced → sent, before acceptance) — while approveChange still accepts a straight priced → approved jump, because a verbal yes on site is common enough that requiring the intermediate step would just get worked around. Added chapterNum so a change's cost/margin effect attributes to the right chapter in the forecast (session 10a's ChangeOrder shape already expected one; it silently defaulted to "1" until now). renderChangeDoc composes the adenda as a customer-facing document with no cost or margin field, the same QUO-10 rule the budget document follows. cancelChange unwinds an un-invoiced change. Applying an approved change's schedule effect to the Gantt is a deliberate separate action (ErpBridge.scheduling.plans.applyChapterDelay) rather than something approval triggers automatically — one action, one system of record.

purchases.note: Session 10b gave the order a real lifecycle (draft → sent → accepted → partial/received → invoiced → paid, plus cancelled) derived from dates and receipts rather than stored as its own field, so it can never fall out of sync with what actually happened. purchaseNeeds() reads the same committedByChapter() the economics screen uses, so "what still needs ordering" can never disagree with "what economía shows as pending". purchaseReconciliation() is the three-way check (order ↔ receipts ↔ invoice) §4.1 asks for. committedCostCents/committedByChapter now include awarded subcontracts too, not just orders — comprometido was always supposed to mean both.

subcontracts.note: New in session 10b — the area had no owner at all before this. One record per awarded trade: awarded/certified/invoiced/pending, mandatory documentation (insurance, PRL, Social Security registration) with a traffic light, retention, and a link to whichever Gantt task executes that trade. markSubcontractStarted BLOCKS — not just alerts — on expired or missing documentation, per §4.2's own "bloqueo ... si está vencida": letting an uninsured trade start on site is the one thing on this screen that should not merely be visible, it should not happen. A terminated subcontract counts as committed only up to what was actually certified, never the full award — the rest of it was never going to be spent.

banking-reconciliation.note: Matching is owned by @repo/capability-reconciliation (src/match.ts) and reached through ErpBridge.reconciliation; erp-engine.js keeps the records and the state transitions. The split follows the same line as project-economics: the engine says what is TRUE (which movements exist, which documents are still open, what a match does to both), and the capability says what is LIKELY (which document explains this line, how sure it is, and why). The 'why' is not decoration — a bare 0,99 next to an Accept button trains people to click without reading, so every suggestion carries the reasons that produced it and the screen renders them. Direction is a gate rather than a weight (a credit can never be explained by a bill), amounts outside tolerance return nothing rather than a weak guess, and a single document always outranks a combination of equal confidence. Session 11 also moved allocation off the Banco screen entirely: casar y repartir is one gesture, and doing it in two places produced movements assigned to a job with no invoice behind them.

labour-hours.note: Session 10b added the weekly grid (worker × day, per §4.6) over the entry recordHours already did, plus what the grid needs to be more than a table: locking (approveLabourWeek/unapproveLabourWeek), "repetir el parte del día anterior" (repeatDay, which never duplicates a worker already logged that day), and worker documentation with its own expiry alert. Recording hours against a closed project is now refused outright rather than merely flagged — the spec's "horas imputadas a un proyecto cerrado" alert can then never actually fire going forward, which is a stronger guarantee than an alert is. correctHours doubles as the reallocation action ("reimputar horas de un proyecto a otro") the spec asks for — a project or chapter change is just another patch, guarded by the same closed-project and locked-week checks.

project-economics.note: Cost at completion is owned by @repo/capability-projects (src/forecast.ts) and reached through ErpBridge.projects.forecast. The split is deliberate and is the whole point of the area: erp-engine.js keeps reporting what HAS happened — the frozen baseline, committed and actual cost, approved change orders, chapter progress — and the capability answers what it IMPLIES. "Spent 40 of a 100 budget" reads as comfortable and says nothing; "spent 40 to get a quarter of the way, so heading for 160" is the sentence somebody can act on, and it did not exist anywhere before. A forecast never comes in below what is already spent or committed, a chapter with nothing booked keeps its budget whatever its progress says (finished-with-no-bill means the bill has not arrived, not that the work was free), and a human override is stored with a required reason and reported ALONGSIDE the calculation rather than replacing it. Nothing moved out of the engine for this to be true.

gestoria-package.note: Session 11 made the quarterly package REFUSABLE. Before, 'Generar y registrar envío' always succeeded and the exception list sat beside it as decoration, which is exactly how a quarter goes out with four suppliers missing a tax id. quarterlyPackage now throws, naming the outstanding items, and the only way past is acceptException with a written justification per item — the two routes §5.6 allows and no third. A force flag was written and then deliberately removed: nobody ever takes one back out. The screen gained the eight completeness blocks (green/amber/red per block, because they fail independently and one aggregate number hides which), the late-document register with duplicate detection against earlier packages, the fixed-asset/vehicle/renting register kept out of site cost, accountant queries, recipient on every send, and a reopen that requires a reason.

alerts-tasks-control-tower.note: Session 12 rebuilt the Torre de Control (§2.1) around the eight cards the spec names — each with a sparkline, a delta against the prior period and a colour dot wired to the SAME numbers the card shows, not a second per-tile threshold store. Every alerts() condition now carries a stable code and a type (económica/técnica/documental/fiscal); ensureAlertRules()/alertRuleThreshold()/alertRuleEnabled() give each one a real enabled/threshold/recipient/channel, configurable from the rule editor, without inventing a second alert engine. managedAlerts() layers assign/due-date/snooze/resolve-with-note-and-evidence/convert-to-task over the pure alerts() projection — the same architecture session 11's gestoría exceptions and comunicaciones queue already established: a computed list plus a keyed overrides map, never a mutated copy. Mi Día (§2.2) gained the hitos calendar via upcomingMilestones(), reading every date off the record that already owns it (project dates, contract installments, bill due dates, purchase arrivals, guarantee expiry, subcontract/worker doc expiry, open tasks, one advisory — explicitly non-legal — gestoría reminder per quarter) rather than a second calendar-specific copy of any of them.

scheduling-gantt.note: Owned by @repo/capability-scheduling and reached only through ErpBridge.scheduling.plans. Session 6 gave it the calendar, CPM and baselines; session 10a added the three things §4.3 asks for around them: the real derivation from the accepted budget (chapters and lines in, durations from quantity divided by the vertical pack's daily output, dependencies chained, re-derivable without losing what the site recorded), the progress curve, and the risk report. Two properties are load-bearing. Derived task ids come from the caller's own references rather than a generator, so re-deriving after a quote change is a merge and not a reset. And the actual-progress curve is drawn from an append-only progress log, never from today's percentages: dates and the critical path recompute from the network at any time, but how much was done by the end of March is only knowable if somebody wrote it down in March.

extraction-ocr.note: Built. @repo/capability-extraction turns recognised text into candidate fields with confidence, provenance and arithmetic checks, and now also a VERDICT per field: green only where a validator vouched for the value — a check digit that computes, a real calendar date, arithmetic that balances — never on confidence alone. site/erp-ocr.js supplies the recognition half (pdf.js text layer first, tesseract.js spa+cat only where there is nothing to read), lazily loaded from site/vendor with no CDN. ADM-03's validation screen writes the record only when a person presses Confirmar, so CAP-04 is enforced by the flow as well as by the capability's confirmed:false type.

journey-project-selector.note: journey.html's existing 'Crear nuevo proyecto' walkthrough (its own sample data, its own "caneiJourney" IndexedDB) is untouched — it stays the default exactly as §2.3 asks. Session 12 added 'Proyecto existente' alongside it, reading the SAME "caneiERP" database erp.html writes, read-only. Rather than re-implement thirteen stages' worth of editing UI a second time in a different language and data shape, each stage shows a real status (completa/en curso/pendiente) and a real summary derived from the record that owns it, plus a link into the actual erp.html screen — "acceso directo a la pantalla real correspondiente ... de modo que el recorrido sirva también como lista de puesta en marcha del proyecto" taken at its word. Switching project asks for confirmation only when it would abandon an in-progress DEMO walkthrough — a read-only real view has nothing local to lose. Duplicating a project makes a real createQuickProject call; downloading a real project's folder reuses the demo's own zipStore/download plumbing with one summary file per stage instead of captured photos.

comunicaciones-templates.note: Templates, rules and the queue, with planning owned by @repo/capability-messaging (src/rules.ts) through ErpBridge.comms. NOTHING SENDS. The rule default is mode:'draft' and that default is the single most important decision in the area — an ERP that mails customers by itself is one bad rule away from an apology, so a rule prepares a message and a person releases it. The engine's commsEvents() is a projection recomputed from current state rather than an append-only log, so a rule added today still sees the invoice that went overdue last week, which is what somebody adding 'chase at 3 days' actually expects. Editing a template mints a new version and retires the old one with supersededBy, so 'which wording did the customer receive' stays answerable.

three-panel-shell.note: Built in session 4, but purely in the view layer of site/erp.html — sections, subsections, the global bar and hash routing. engineSection is null because there is no business rule here to own: the shell reads counts and alerts through the same engine calls the views already use. Recorded as 'engine' rather than 'unbuilt' because it exists and is in use; there is no owner value for 'view-only'.

task-status-summary.note: First area served by the capability layer. Task counts by status are computed by @repo/capability-scheduling via site/erp-bridge.js, not by ad-hoc filtering in the view. The underlying task records are still owned by erp-engine.js (see alerts-tasks-control-tower) — only this derivation moved, which is what made it safe to land first.

reconciliation-matching.note: The capability itself: @repo/capability-reconciliation. Scores a bank line against the open documents that could explain it — exact and near amounts, same and near dates, a reference quoted in the free text, a counterparty named in it — and returns suggestions carrying their own reasons. Combinations up to three documents cover the one-transfer-pays-two-invoices case, and internal transfers are detected as mirrored pairs across accounts so they stop counting as income and expense. Zero jurisdiction or sector knowledge: it knows amounts, dates, directions and strings.
